authored_by: the C# port, by hand, against the published Rules Reference
notes: Card abilities as data -- docs/card-dsl.md. A card listed here has been read; one with an empty 'abilities' has been read and found to do nothing, which is a different thing from nobody having looked at it. Printed text is quoted from datasets/cards/cards.json, which is extracted rather than authored. The Rules Reference decides every behaviour here; where a card's printed words do not settle a case, the note on that card says so and says what was chosen instead.

cards.name: Spider-Man
cards.note: Spider-Sense -- Interrupt: When the villain initiates an attack against you, draw 1 card. 'You' is the attacked player and not the attacked character: rr:attack-enemy-activation.1.4. Printed on the hero face only, which is why the alter-ego face 01001b is a separate card id and carries its own.

cards.name: Peter Parker
cards.note: Scientist -- Resource: Generate a [mental] resource. (Limit once per round.) The sixth generator in the recorded prompt, and the reason that prompt lists six for five payable cards: rr:resource-ability.1 makes one triggerable 'anytime the player who controls the ability is generating resources to pay a cost', so it sits beside the cards in hand rather than in a window. rr:limit counts the use per instance of the ability, which is per card in play -- two Peter Parkers at one table would have one use each.

cards.name: Black Cat
cards.note: Forced Response: After you play Black Cat, discard the top 2 cards of your deck. Add each card with a printed mental resource discarded this way to your hand. The remembered set belongs to this one resolution; rr:printed requires the resource printed on the card, not a modifier.

cards.name: Backflip
cards.note: Interrupt (defense): When you would take any amount of damage from an attack, prevent all of that damage. The attack-damage step carries rr:damage.step.1's imminent-damage condition, and the one-use replacement is consumed by that damage only.

cards.name: Enhanced Spider-Sense
cards.note: Hero Interrupt: When a treachery card is revealed from the encounter deck, cancel its When Revealed effects. rr:cancel.4 leaves the treachery revealed and discarded; only its When Revealed effects are skipped.

cards.name: Swinging Web Kick
cards.note: Hero Action (attack): Deal 8 damage to an enemy. Triggering the Action plays this event under rr:player-turn.5.d, paying its printed cost and discarding it after the chosen enemy is damaged.

cards.name: Spider-Tracer
cards.note: Attach to a minion. Forced Interrupt: When attached minion is defeated, remove 3 threat from a scheme. The chosen scheme is resolved after the defeat interrupt and may be either the main scheme or a side scheme.

cards.name: Web-Shooter
cards.note: Uses (3 web counters). Hero Resource: Exhaust Web-Shooter and remove 1 web counter from it to generate a wild resource. rr:uses-x-type discards the card when its last all-purpose counter is removed.

cards.name: Webbed Up
cards.note: Hero form only. Attach to an enemy. Max 1 per enemy. Forced Interrupt: When attached enemy would attack, discard Webbed Up instead. Then, stun that enemy. The WhenAttackInitiated interrupt precedes attack application, so the newly stunned actor's attack is cancelled by rr:stun.

cards.name: Charge
cards.note: Attach to Rhino. [star] Forced Interrupt: When Rhino attacks, the attack gains overkill. At the end of this attack, discard Charge. The star sits in this card's ATK field, which rr:star-icon.2 makes a reminder to check the text box whenever the attached enemy uses that value to attack -- so this is an attachment ability while in play, not a 'Boost' ability. The printed ATK+ 3 is not here: rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier declarative, and StateFields reads it off the attachment without an ability. 'Rhino' is written as the villain in play because the card belongs to Rhino's encounter set and no other villain can share a table with it; a name query would need a lookup the printed data spells differently.

cards.name: "I'm Tough"
cards.note: When Revealed: Give Rhino a tough status card. If Rhino already has a tough status card, this card gains surge. The no-villain case is not printed and no rule covers it. **Our choice:** surge. A reveal that neither gives a status card nor surges is a card that does nothing at all, and rr:surge.1 is the branch the card already prints for 'the tough status card could not be given'. Both branches run: `giveStatus` is capped by rr:status-cards.1 and `gainSurge` deals one encounter card, which is rr:surge.1's 'When Revealed: deal yourself 1 facedown encounter card'.

cards.name: Advance
cards.note: When Revealed: The villain schemes. rr:scheme is the fifth basic power and this is the villain using it outside its own activation, so it is scheduled as a Scheme step rather than resolved here. It is a scheme however the revealing player's form would have activated the villain: rr:activation.1 decides the *scheduled* activation of the villain phase, and this card has already decided.

cards.name: Assault
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): This card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): The villain attacks you. Two printed abilities gated on form, written as one 'if' because the two forms are exclusive: the parenthesis is a condition on the ability rather than two abilities that could both apply. 'You' is the player revealing the card, which is the seat the When Revealed occurrence carries.

cards.name: Gang-Up
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): This card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): The villain and each minion engaged with you attacks you. Two activations rather than one attack by several enemies -- rr:attack-enemy-activation is one enemy's -- and a minion engaged with you attacking is the same thing villain phase step 2.b would have done. The order is the play area's, for the reason rr:minion.3 is taken that way there.

cards.name: Shocker
cards.note: When Revealed: Deal 1 damage to each hero. A minion, so the card also enters play; the ability is what the reveal resolves. 'Each hero' is not each identity -- rr:form-change-form.5 says abilities that interact with a player's hero do not interact with the identity of a player in alter-ego form, so a player who has flipped down takes nothing.

cards.name: Breakin' & Takin'
cards.note: When Revealed: Place an additional 1 [per_hero] threat here. 'Additional' is additional to the printed starting threat, which rr:side-scheme.1 has already placed by the time this resolves -- so this places only what the text says and does not restate the 2. 'Here' is the card itself. The hazard icon is a printed field and not this ability.

cards.name: Bomb Scare
cards.note: When Revealed: Place an additional 1 [per_hero] threat here. Word for word Breakin' & Takin', from a different encounter set; the acceleration icon rather than the hazard icon is the difference, and both are printed fields rather than abilities.

cards.name: Hard to Keep Down
cards.note: When Revealed: Rhino heals 4 damage. If no damage was healed this way, this card gains surge. The condition reads result.healed and not the villain's health, because rr:heal heals up to the amount: a villain damaged by 1 heals 1 and one at full health heals nothing, and a check made before the heal reads a number the heal may never reach. A villain that is not on the board heals nothing, which is the surge branch and not an error.

cards.name: False Alarm
cards.note: When Revealed: You are confused. If you are already confused, this card gains surge. 'You' is a card here and not a player: rr:you-your.5 says a status card placed on 'you' goes on the resolving player's identity. Written as if/else on the same shape as 01105 -- rr:status-cards.1 caps a character at one card of each type, so the two branches are exclusive in fact as well as in the sentence.

cards.name: Hydra Bomber
cards.note: When Revealed: Choose to either take 2 damage or place 1 threat on the main scheme. rr:choose-game-element.1 asks the player resolving the ability, which for a revealed encounter card is the player it was dealt to. rr:you-your.2 makes 'take 2 damage' damage to that player's identity. Neither option needs a target beyond one that is always there, so rr:choose-option.1 -- an encounter card cannot offer an option with no valid target -- never bites here.

cards.name: Rhino
cards.note: Stage I. No text at all: the printed HP, ATK, SCH and the Boost field are attributes rather than abilities, and rr:attachment.1 makes the printed modifiers on what is attached to him declarative too. Read and empty, which is not the same as unread.

cards.name: Hydra Mercenary
cards.note: Guard, and nothing else. rr:guard is a keyword the engine reads off the printed field -- see docs/keywords.md -- so there is no ability here to author.

cards.name: Sandman
cards.note: Toughness, and nothing else. rr:toughness gives the minion a tough status card as it enters play, which Reveal.EnterPlay does from the printed keyword.

cards.name: Crowd Control
cards.note: A crisis icon and no text. rr:crisis-icon.1 makes the icon 'equivalent to the following constant ability: player cards cannot remove threat from the main scheme', and the engine reads it off the printed field in BasicPowers -- a constant ability is not a triggered one and has nothing to wait for.

cards.name: The Break-In!
cards.note: Stage 1B. 'If this stage is completed, the players lose the game' is rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.2.1 restated on the card, and the engine answers it in Threat.Completed: an empty main scheme deck under a completed scheme is the villain winning. Nothing here to trigger.

cards.name: Caught Off Guard
cards.note: When Revealed: Discard an upgrade or support you control. If no cards were discarded this way, this card gains surge. Written as if/else on whether there is one, rather than as a discard followed by a check: the instruction is mandatory, so 'no cards were discarded this way' happens exactly when there was nothing to discard. That also keeps the choice last in its branch, which is what the interpreter can resume. rr:choose-game-element.1 asks the player resolving the card, which is the player it was dealt to.

cards.name: Rhino
cards.note: Stage II. When Revealed: Search the encounter deck and discard pile for the Breakin' & Takin' side scheme and reveal it. Shuffle the encounter deck. The final sentence is rr:search.3 restated -- 'if any portion of a deck is searched, upon completion of that card ability, shuffle that entire deck' -- so it is the node's own doing rather than a second instruction. The discard pile is searched and not shuffled, because it is not a deck. Named by printed id because the card names a specific card and rr:identity.2 makes a title refer to one card.

cards.name: Exhaustion
cards.note: Surge. When Revealed: Exhaust your identity card. The surge is a printed keyword the engine already reads, so the ability is the one sentence. 'Your identity card' is rr:you-your again -- the resolving player's identity, whichever face is showing, and rr:form-change-form.2 keeps the exhausted state across a flip.

cards.name: Under Fire
cards.note: Surge. When Revealed: Reveal the top card of the encounter deck. Revealed and not dealt -- rr:deal-deal-an-encounter-card puts a card facedown in a queue for the next villain phase, and this one is turned over now. The surge deals a card as well, so this treachery costs two: one revealed at once and one queued.

cards.name: Shadow of the Past
cards.note: When Revealed: Reveal your set-aside nemesis minion and put it into play engaged with you. Reveal your set-aside nemesis side scheme and put it into play. Shuffle the rest of your set-aside nemesis encounter set into the encounter deck. If your nemesis minion does not enter the game this way, this card gains surge. The card appears in 132 of the 135 campaigns in the dataset, more than any other encounter card. 'Put into play engaged with you' and 'put it into play' are both rr:reveal.step.2 by card type, so both are a reveal rather than a placement. The two reveals happen before the shuffle so that the cards they take are no longer among 'the rest'; the obligation is not among them either, because setup shuffled it into the encounter deck long before this resolves.

cards.name: Masterplan
cards.note: When Revealed: Place 4 threat on each side scheme. If there are no side schemes in play, discard cards from the top of the encounter deck until a side scheme is discarded. Reveal that side scheme. Written as if/else because the sentence is one: 'each side scheme' when there are any, the search when there are none. 'Each side scheme' reaches the players' as well as the scenario's -- rr:player-side-scheme calls them the player card equivalent and .1 puts them in the same place. Four threat flat, not per player.

cards.name: Vulture
cards.note: Quickstrike, and nothing else. Spider-Man's nemesis minion, brought in by Shadow of the Past. rr:quickstrike is a keyword the engine reads off the printed field, so there is no ability here to author.

cards.name: Stampede
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): This card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): Rhino attacks you. If a character is damaged by this attack, that character is stunned. The second sentence is a delayed effect and not a response: rr:delayed-effect.1 resolves it immediately after the condition becomes true and before responses to it may be used, and rr:delayed-effect.2 says it is not a new triggered ability. The character it stuns does not exist when the effect is made -- the attack has not happened -- so the occurrence names it when it comes due. rr:tough.3 is why 'damaged' is not 'attacked': a character whose tough status card ate the damage is not considered to have taken damage, and is not stunned.

cards.name: Sweeping Swoop
cards.note: When Revealed: Stun your hero. If Vulture is in play, this card gains surge. [star] Boost: If this activation deals damage to a friendly character, stun that character. Two abilities at two tiers on one card, which is why the boost guard asks whether *this half* is written rather than whether the card is. 'Your hero' is not 'you': rr:form-change-form.5 says abilities that interact with a player's hero do not interact with the identity of a player in alter-ego form, so an alter-ego is not stunned -- and the surge branch is a separate sentence that still applies. The boost half is bounded by the end of the activation rather than the end of the attack, because a scheme is an activation too and an effect that outlived one would fire during somebody else's attack. Every character an enemy activation damages is friendly, so the boost's 'friendly' needs no filter of its own; a card that damages an enemy this way would.

cards.name: Aunt May
cards.note: Alter-Ego Action: Exhaust Aunt May -> heal 4 damage from Peter Parker. The first card in the dataset with a cost, and the first with an action. rr:player-turn.5.1 is the 'Alter-Ego' in front of it: the player must be in that form to trigger it, which is the trigger's 'form'. rr:initiating-abilities keeps the steps apart, so the exhaust is the ability's cost rather than the first thing its effect does -- and rr:exhausted.2 is why an already-exhausted Aunt May is not offered at all. 'Peter Parker' is the player's identity: the card is in their play area and rr:you-your resolves the alter-ego by title to the identity showing it.

cards.name: Enhanced Ivory Horn
cards.note: Attach to Rhino. Hero Action: Spend [physical] [physical] [physical] resources -> discard this card. An encounter card in play, so rr:player-turn.5.b is what lets a player trigger it -- it is nobody's card and everybody's action. The printed ATK+ 1 is not here: rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier declarative and StateFields reads it off the attachment without an ability. The spend is the ability's cost rather than the first thing its effect does, which is why rr:initiating-abilities.step.3 can refuse to offer it to a hand that cannot pay.

cards.name: The Vulture's Plans
cards.note: When Revealed: Discard 1 card at random from each player's hand. Place 1 threat on the main scheme for each different resource type discarded this way. 'Each player' goes in player order -- rr:each-player.1 -- and that order is what the random stream sees, so it is a wire fact rather than a tidiness. 'Each different resource type' counts distinct letters among what was discarded: a card printing two of one letter is one type and a card printing none is none, so the threat is between zero and four however many players there are.

cards.name: Eviction Notice
cards.note: Give to the Peter Parker player. You may flip to alter-ego form. Choose: exhaust Peter Parker to remove Eviction Notice from the game, or discard 1 card at random from your hand, this card gains surge, discard this obligation. Two questions in a row, which is the shape the interpreter had to learn to resume for. rr:form-change-form.3 is why the flip does not use up the turn's: 'if a card ability causes a player to change forms, it does not count against the one voluntary form change'. rr:obligation.1 makes 'you' the player whose play area the obligation is in, which rr:obligation.4 makes the Peter Parker player -- the same seat as the revealing player at one player, and MARVEL-225 above two. The first option's exhaust is written as its effect rather than as a cost because rr:choose-option.1 bars an encounter card's option only for want of a target, not for want of a cost.

cards.name: Explosion
cards.note: When Revealed: If Bomb Scare is in play, assign X damage among heroes and allies, where X is the amount of threat on Bomb Scare. If Bomb Scare is not in play, this card gains surge. X is read off the board rather than printed -- rr:threat counts tokens -- so it is the threat pool on the card named by title. The assignment is rr:indirect-damage: .2 divides it among friendly characters in play, .3 assigns the whole lot before resolving any of it, and .3.1 caps each character at its remaining hit points. Only two cards in the pool say 'assign ... among' and the other one says 'indirect' outright; this one does not, but the division it describes is the same one.

cards.name: Highway Robbery
cards.note: When Revealed: Each player places a random card from their hand facedown here. When Defeated: Return each facedown card here to its owner's hand. Placed and not discarded -- the cards come back, which is what the second ability is for -- so they go onto the scheme as attachments, facedown. 'Its owner's hand' is the card's owner and not whoever defeated the scheme, which is why each player gets their own card back. rr:when-defeated-abilities.2.1 runs the return before the scheme leaves play, which is what lets it still find what is attached to it.

cards.name: Armored Rhino Suit
cards.note: Attach to Rhino. Forced Interrupt: When any amount of damage would be dealt to Rhino, place it here instead. Then, if there is at least 5 damage here, discard Armored Rhino Suit. A replacement effect -- rr:replacement-effect's 'when [triggering condition] would happen, do [replacement effect] instead' -- sitting at rr:damage.step.1, which is before the tough card at step 2. 'Place it here' is placing and not dealing: the damage goes on as tokens rather than starting the nine steps again on a card that is not a character. The subject is the attached card rather than this one, because it is Rhino being dealt the damage.

cards.name: Rhino
cards.note: Stage III, which only the expert villain deck reaches. Toughness is a printed keyword rather than an ability -- rr:toughness.1 spells it out as a Forced Response and Reveal.EnterPlay is where the engine keeps it -- so the When Revealed is all there is to author. 'Each hero' is rr:form-change-form.5: while a player is in alter-ego form, card abilities that interact with their hero do not interact with their identity, so a table that has flipped down takes nothing.

cards.name: The Break-In!
cards.note: Main scheme stage 1, the A side. Its printed text is the scenario's contents list and one setup line, 'Advance to stage 1B.' Neither is an ability this card runs: the contents say what to put in the box before the game, and the advance is the setup step itself. rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.12.b flips the main scheme to side 1B for every scenario, and the engine does it there -- so this line is that rule restated on the card, in the same category as 01097b's 'the players lose the game'. It is deliberately not authored as a Setup ability: running it at step 12a would advance the scheme and step 12b would then advance it again, off the end of a deck that has one stage in it. Sixty-two main schemes in the pool print the clause and the appendix covers all of them. rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.step.2 and .step.3 are the same two-sided reveal for a stage the deck advances to, and 01097b is where that side's text lives. Read and empty, which is not the same as unread.

cards.name: Boomerang
cards.note: Forced Response: After Boomerang attacks you, deal 1 damage to each ally you control. [star] Boost: Deal 2 damage to an ally you control. The response is on rr:attack-enemy-activation.step.6.a -- 'the attack finishes resolving and the following types of abilities trigger in order: forced abilities with the following triggers ... after [character] attacks [and damages/defeats] [you/an ally]' -- so it waits for the whole attack rather than firing at the damage step. Actor 'this' says Boomerang made the attack; who 'you' is comes from the occurrence rather than from the trigger, which is rr:you-your.7 -- 'for abilities that trigger after [enemy] attacks you, you refers to the attacked player, even if that player defended with an ally' -- and rr:attack-enemy-activation.1.4 says the same thing about which character was targeted. The boost half is guarded by exists: rr:choose-game-element has nothing to choose when the player controls no ally, and a card that asks anyway would stop the game on a board where the answer is 'nothing happens'.

cards.name: Beetle
cards.note: Forced Response: After Beetle attacks and damages you, discard the lowest-cost upgrade you control. [star] Boost: Choose and discard an upgrade you control. 'And damages' is a second fact about the same attack, and rr:attack-enemy-activation.step.6.a's abilities all run after the attack is over -- so the attack records whether it landed and attackDamaged reads it. rr:tough.3 is what makes it come apart in an ordinary game: a character whose tough status card absorbed the attack 'is not considered to have taken damage', so Beetle attacked and did not damage. The response takes the lowest-cost upgrade through chooseCard rather than straight, because the Rules Reference gives no tie-break for 'the lowest-cost X' and minBy keeps ties -- with one candidate the question has one answer, which is what Caught Off Guard's choice already does. rr:permanent.4.1 names this shape outright and Ranked drops permanents before comparing, so a cheap permanent cannot shield a dearer upgrade.

cards.name: White Rabbit
cards.note: [star] Forced Interrupt: When White Rabbit attacks you, discard 1 card at random from your hand. [star] Boost: Choose and discard 1 identity-specific card from your hand. The interrupt is timed to the attack initiating, which rr:attack-enemy-activation.5 puts with 'interrupts that trigger when [an enemy] initiates an attack' -- so the card goes before the boost card is even given, and a card the player might have wanted to pay with is gone before they are asked to defend. 'Your hand' is the attacked player's: rr:you-your.7 makes 'you' the attacked player for a trigger of this shape, and the interpreter takes it from the occurrence rather than from who owns the card. The boost half is guarded by exists because rr:choose-game-element has nothing to offer a hand with no identity-specific card in it, which is an ordinary hand rather than an edge case.

cards.name: Sinister Onslaught
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): Each [[Criminal]] enemy in play schemes. If no enemy schemed this way, this card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): Each [[Criminal]] enemy in play attacks you. If no enemy attacked this way, this card gains surge. Written as one ability with a form test rather than two, the way Assault is: the parenthesis is a condition on the ability and the forms are exclusive, so a card with both would fire twice. 'If no enemy attacked this way' is the same query asked before the fact rather than a count taken after: every enemy the query names does activate -- rr:activation.1 chooses between attacking and scheming by the player's form and the card has already chosen -- so an empty query and a count of zero are the same board. The trait is written as the engine spells it -- CRIMINAL, upper case, with spaces underscored -- which is the same rule the trigger vocabulary follows: a translation table between what a card prints and what the engine stores is a second vocabulary, and a second vocabulary drifts. Rhino himself carries the Criminal trait, so on the scenario this set is dealt into the surge branch is the rare one; it is reached when the villain is somehow not in play.

cards.name: Crime Pays
cards.note: When Revealed: Search the encounter deck for a [[Criminal]] minion and put it into play engaged with you. (Shuffle.) If no minion was put into play this way, this card gains surge. Three rules meet on this card. rr:search.1 gives the player the choice when several cards match, which is a chooseCard over what the search found rather than the interpreter picking. rr:search.3 shuffles 'upon completion of that game step, game function, or card ability' -- after the answer, and in both branches, because the deck was searched whether or not anything was found. And rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 is why the minion is put into play rather than revealed: 'if an encounter card with a When Revealed ability is put into play without being revealed, the When Revealed ability does not trigger.' Its keywords still fire, because rr:enters-play is 'any time when a card transitions from an out-of-play area into play' and a card put into play does. The trait is the engine's spelling.

cards.name: Shocker
cards.note: Forced Response: After Shocker is attacked, stun the attacking character. [star] Boost: Stun the character you control with the highest ATK value. The response is rr:attack-player-ability-type.step.7, which lists 'after [character] is attacked' among the forced abilities an attack's resolution triggers -- and it is the reason a character's basic attack is a step of the agenda at all rather than a call that returns. The target is Shocker and the actor is the attacking character. That actor is a character and not a player: rr:ally.2 lets a player attack with an ally and rr:you-your.15 says an ally's attack is not performed by that player's identity. The boost half goes through chooseCard because maxBy keeps ties and the Rules Reference gives no tie-break for 'the highest X'; an alter-ego prints no ATK and rr:dash-value.3 makes that an unmodifiable 0, so a table in alter-ego form still has a highest.

cards.name: Speed Demon
cards.note: Forced Interrupt: When a character attacks Speed Demon, Speed Demon attacks that character. (Resolve Speed Demon's attack first.) [star] Boost: Discard the lowest-cost support you control. The parenthesis is a real instruction and not a reminder, which is why it is recorded. rr:interrupt.1 resolves an interrupt before the occurrence it answers, and the ability does resolve there -- but its effect is itself an activation, and rr:activation.8 sends one of those to the back: 'an activation initiated during another resolves after the current activation has finished resolving.' So without 'first' the counter-attack would land after the attack it is answering, which is the reading the card prints the parenthesis to rule out. 'That character' is the attacker rather than the player, and Speed Demon attacking an ally is rr:attack-enemy-activation.1.1's exception: 'abilities can instead cause an enemy to attack a player's alter-ego or an ally that player controls.' rr:attacks-against-allies.1 keeps the player attacked either way, so the seat does not move. The boost half says support and not upgrade, and the two are separate queries for that reason; rr:permanent.4.1 names 'discard the lowest-cost support you control' as its own worked example, and Ranked drops permanents before comparing.

cards.name: Unus
cards.note: Toughness. If the amount of threat on Gene Pool is at least: 3 -- Unus gains retaliate 1. 6 -- Unus also gains stalwart. 9 -- Unus also gains a [amplify] icon. Toughness is a printed keyword the engine already reads, so nothing is written for it. The rest is one constant ability: rr:ability.5 -- no bold timing trigger -- and specifically rr:ability.9, 'some constant abilities continuously seek a specific condition (denoted by words such as during, if, or while). The effects of such abilities are active anytime the specific condition is met.' So the three clauses are re-read every time anything asks what is in force, and Unus loses retaliate the moment Gene Pool is thwarted below three threat. 'Also' makes them cumulative rather than a ladder: at nine threat all three are in force, which is why they are three independent tests and not an if/else chain. Gene Pool is named by title and rr:identity.2 makes a title name one card. The three stages print the same ability and each is authored separately, because a stage is a card.

cards.name: Flight
cards.note: Setup. Attach to the villain. Permanent. The attach-to is rr:attach-to, a rule about the phrase rather than an ability, so it is the card's attachTo and not a When Revealed -- rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 would not fire one on a card put into play by rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.11 without being revealed. Permanent and the printed ATK+ 1 are declarative: rr:permanent is a printed field and rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier something StateFields reads off the attachment without an ability. What is left is one constant ability -- rr:ability.5, no bold timing trigger -- and rr:ability.9 keeps it in force only while the card is in play. Attached villain gains the AERIAL trait. [star] Attached villain's attacks gain overkill. The star sits in the ATK field, which rr:star-icon.2 makes a reminder to check the text box whenever the attached enemy uses that value to attack -- so the overkill is about the villain's attacks. Granting it to the villain outright is the same thing here and not a shortcut: rr:overkill is only ever asked of the attacker during an attack, and nothing else in the engine asks whether a character has it.

cards.name: Super Strength
cards.note: Setup. Attach to the villain. Permanent. The attach-to is rr:attach-to, a rule about the phrase rather than an ability, so it is the card's attachTo and not a When Revealed -- rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 would not fire one on a card put into play by rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.11 without being revealed. Permanent and the printed ATK+ 1 are declarative: rr:permanent is a printed field and rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier something StateFields reads off the attachment without an ability. What is left is one constant ability -- rr:ability.5, no bold timing trigger -- and rr:ability.9 keeps it in force only while the card is in play. Attached villain gains the BRUTE trait and steady. Steady is a printed field the engine already reads -- rr:status-cards.1.1 lets a steady character have one additional confused and one additional stunned status card, and Statuses.Limit asks through StateFields.Modified -- so granting it is adding to that field.

cards.name: Telepathy
cards.note: Setup. Attach to the villain. Permanent. The attach-to is rr:attach-to, a rule about the phrase rather than an ability, so it is the card's attachTo and not a When Revealed -- rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 would not fire one on a card put into play by rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.11 without being revealed. Permanent and the printed SCH+ 1 are declarative: rr:permanent is a printed field and rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier something StateFields reads off the attachment without an ability. What is left is one constant ability -- rr:ability.5, no bold timing trigger -- and rr:ability.9 keeps it in force only while the card is in play. Attached villain gains the PSIONIC trait and retaliate 1. Retaliate carries a number where steady does not, which is why the grant states one: rr:retaliate-x deals X damage to the attacker, and Damage.Retaliate reads X through StateFields.Modified.

cards.name: Hunting Gene Traitors
cards.note: Contents line, then 'Setup: Reveal the Gene Pool side scheme. In expert mode, deal each player a facedown encounter card.' The contents line is what to put in the box before the game and not an ability. The Gene Pool clause is not written, and deliberately: 45071 Gene Pool prints the setup keyword itself, so rr:setup-keyword.1 has already put it into play by the time rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.12.a runs -- the two printings are one card entering play once, and revealing it here would put it in twice. Same category as 'Advance to stage 1B' on 01097a: a rule the engine already keeps, restated on the card. The expert clause is real and is what is written. rr:deal leaves a dealt card facedown for step 4 of the villain phase to turn over, so these wait for the first villain phase rather than resolving during setup.

cards.name: Hunting Gene Traitors
cards.note: [star] Forced Response: After resolving step one of the villain phase, place 1 threat on Gene Pool. If this scheme is completed, the players lose the game. The second line is rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.2.1 restated and Threat.Completed answers it, the same as 01097b. Step one of the villain phase is rr:villain-phase.step.1, which places threat on the main scheme -- the engine's PlaceThreat step, and the only thing that produces WhenThreatPlaced. The star sits on the main scheme, so this is its ability -- but the subject is 'game' and not 'this': the step places threat on the main scheme without the occurrence naming it, because 'after resolving step one of the villain phase' names a moment and nothing in it. Gene Pool is named by title and rr:identity.2 makes a title name one card.

cards.name: Culling the Weak
cards.note: When Revealed: Place 4 threat on Gene Pool. [star] Boost: Place 2 threat on Gene Pool. Two abilities on one card and the same effect twice, which rr:boost-boost-icon.2 keeps apart: the boost half resolves only when the card is turned faceup as a boost card, and the reveal half only when it is revealed. Gene Pool is named by title -- rr:identity.2 makes a title name one card -- rather than by printed id, because the side scheme belongs to the Infinites encounter set and more than one scenario uses it.

cards.name: Endless Ranks
cards.note: When Defeated: Place 3 threat on Gene Pool. rr:when-defeated-abilities.1 defines the timing as exactly 'Forced Interrupt: When this card is defeated', and .2.1 keeps the card in play while it resolves -- so the scheme is still on the table as the threat goes onto Gene Pool. The printed starting threat and the acceleration icon are fields rather than abilities.

cards.name: War-Weary
cards.note: When Revealed: You are stunned. If you were already stunned, take 2 damage instead. [star] Boost: the same. 'Instead' is why this is one if and not two sentences: rr:replacement-effect reads 'instead' as the damage taking the stun's place, so a player who is already stunned does not also gain a second status card. rr:you-your.5 -- 'if a card ability places a status card on you, the player resolving that card ability places that status card on their identity' -- so both halves name the identity, which is what 'you' resolves to.

cards.name: Infinite Soldier
cards.note: Guard. If the amount of threat on Gene Pool is at least: 3 -- this minion gains quickstrike. 6 -- also surge. 9 -- also +3 hit points. Guard is a printed field the engine already reads. The rest is Unus's own shape one card down: rr:ability.9, 'some constant abilities continuously seek a specific condition [...] the effects of such abilities are active anytime the specific condition is met', so the three clauses are re-read on every ask and 'also' makes them cumulative rather than a ladder. Hit points are granted as health, which is computed rather than printed -- remaining hit points are printed HP less damage -- but Damage.Health sums modifiers into it, which is what +3 hit points means.

cards.name: Targeted for Extermination
cards.note: When Defeated: The player who defeated this scheme confuses their identity. The crisis icon and the printed starting threat are fields rather than abilities. 'The player who defeated' is not the card's owner and not the first player: a side scheme is defeated by the character that removed its last threat, and rr:ownership-and-control.2 puts that character under its owner's control -- so an ally thwarting it is still that player's doing, which rr:you-your.15 keeps off their identity as a separate question. rr:you-your.5 is why the status lands on the identity: a status card placed on a player goes there.

cards.name: Gene Pool
cards.note: Permanent. Setup. Forced Response: After an ally is defeated by anything other than consequential damage, place 3 threat here. The two keywords are not written: rr:setup-keyword puts the card into play during setup and rr:permanent keeps it there, and both are printed keywords the engine already reads. What is written is the response. 'An ally' is any ally and not this card's, so the trigger's subject is the game rather than a card -- rr:triggering-condition makes the occurrence the thing that happened, and what happened is that somebody's ally died. 'By anything other than consequential damage' is the only negative condition in this dataset, and it reads exactly as printed: not a list of the causes that do count, which would go stale the moment a set added another one, but the one cause that does not. rr:consequential-damage is the rule it names; the interpreter is what knows which verb the engine records that under. rr:ability.7 makes a Forced Response mandatory, so there is nothing to offer and no cost.

cards.name: Infinite Hunter
cards.note: When Revealed: Deal 3 damage to an ally you control. [star] Boost: Choose to either place 2 threat on Gene Pool, or the activating enemy gets +2 SCH and +2 ATK for this activation. Two abilities on one card, kept apart by rr:boost-boost-icon.2, and the first card in this dataset with a choice in each -- which is why a suspended choice now carries the tier it came from. 'An ally you control' is where the card is: rr:play-area.1 puts a player's cards in their own play area. With no ally the reveal does nothing, guarded by exists, because rr:choose-game-element has nothing to choose from and the card names no alternative. The boost half is the first card to name the activating enemy: a boost card is turned faceup in the middle of an activation and its own occurrence is about the boost card, so the enemy is read off the board. rr:activation is why one answer serves both kinds. EndOfActivation rather than EndOfAttack is the duration because rr:activation.6 gives an activation an end and a scheme is not an attack -- a +2 that outlived a scheme would go off during somebody's attack, against somebody it was never about. SCH and ATK are two grants because the engine reads two fields.

cards.name: Hunted
cards.note: Alter-Ego Action: Discard a card from your hand -> discard this card. An obligation, so rr:reveal.4 puts it into the revealing player's play area and it stays there; the printed hazard icon is a field the engine already reads and the whole of the card's text is this one way out. The cost is the first in this dataset that is not resources: rr:cost.3 spends resources by discarding cards from hand, and this discards a card from hand without reading what it would have generated -- a card with no printed RES pays it, and a card printing two does not pay twice. So the payment is a chosen card rather than a number, which is why it travels as a target: rr:initiating-abilities keeps step 2's choosing and step 5's paying apart, and the answer carries both separately. rr:player-turn.5.1 is the Alter-Ego, checked where every action's form is.

cards.name: Prelate Sidearm
cards.note: Attach to Unus. [star] Forced Response: After Unus attacks and defeats an ally, place 1 threat on Gene Pool. Hero Response: After you make a basic attack against Unus, spend [energy] [physical] resources -> discard this card. The second half is 45064 Prelate Armor's, two letters different. The first is the sentence rr:triggering-condition.2 makes writable: 'attacks and defeats' is one occurrence carrying two conditions -- 'a single attack causing a character to both take damage and be defeated' -- so the card answers the defeat and reads the attack actor from the same occurrence. Actor attachedTo says Unus made the attack; an ally killed by its own consequential damage has no attack actor, and one killed by Unus's retaliate has Unus as the target rather than the actor. alsoHappened requires the attack's damage condition as well as the defeat. Gene Pool is named by title -- rr:identity.2 makes a title name one card. The [star] ATK+1 and Boost 3 are printed fields rather than abilities.

cards.name: Prelate Armor
cards.note: Attach to Unus. [star] Forced Response: After Unus schemes, give him a tough status card. Hero Response: After you make a basic attack against Unus, spend [mental] [physical] resources -> discard this card. The star is rr:star-icon.2 -- the ability is about the attached enemy -- so both triggers name attachedTo rather than this, the same as 01099 Charge. 'After Unus schemes' is the end of the activation and not its start: the threat goes on the main scheme in between, and rr:attack-enemy-activation keeps the same two moments apart on the other kind -- 'when [enemy name] attacks' is the initiation and .step.6.a is where the abilities that ask what it did live. The second is 01100 Enhanced Ivory Horn one tier over: the same attachment, the same arrow cost, the same discard, timed to a response instead of an action. rr:cost-arrow-icon puts the payment before the effect, and rr:initiating-abilities.step.5 pays it. Two things the window had never been asked for and an action always had: whose form to read -- step 2, and a Hero Response is as much a form requirement as a Hero Action -- and whose hand to price it against. rr:you-your.7 answers both by pointing at the player the occurrence happened to, which is what the trigger's 'player' says. The [star] SCH+1 and Boost 3 are printed fields rather than abilities.

cards.name: The Doomsday Chair
cards.note: When Revealed: If M.O.D.O.K. is not in play, search the encounter deck and discard pile for M.O.D.O.K. and put him into play engaged with you, then shuffle the encounter deck. The title check reads only in-play areas, so a copy in either searched out-of-play area does not suppress the effect. rr:search.1 makes a matching card the player's choice if more than one exists; the core set has one M.O.D.O.K., and singular cardsIn refuses rather than guesses if a future board produces several. rr:search.2 leaves every card where it is until putIntoPlay moves the match. rr:search.3 requires the encounter deck shuffle even when no match exists, so both branches say it. And rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 is why the move is putIntoPlay rather than reveal: a When Revealed ability on M.O.D.O.K. would not trigger, while rr:enters-play still applies its printed keywords.

cards.name: M.O.D.O.K.
cards.note: Retaliate 2. The card has no authored ability because Retaliate is a printed keyword read by the rules engine. rr:retaliate-x makes it a Forced Response after this character is attacked, and rr:retaliate-x.2 requires M.O.D.O.K. to remain in play after the attack resolves.

cards.name: Biomechanical Upgrades
cards.note: Surge. Attach to the minion with the highest printed hit points and without another Biomechanical Upgrades attached. Forced Interrupt: When attached minion would be defeated, heal all damage from it instead, then discard this card. The surge is a printed keyword the reveal rule reads. The attachment selector uses printed HP rather than modified HP; the official ruling in datasets/marvelcdb-faq/faq.json says base stats on a facedown Ultron drone count as printed and '+ stats' do not. rr:first-player.1 gives a tied highest target to the first player, which the engine refuses until attachment selection can ask. rr:damage.step.6 places this interrupt after damage is placed and before defeat, so healing all damage invalidates the imminent defeat under rr:would.1. The final discard then removes this copy from play under rr:attach-to.1.
